nodes.name: Finite-valued weighted clone
nodes.statement: A weighted clone $W$ on $D$ is called \emph{finite-valued} if the support clone of $W$ is $\mathbf{I}_D$.
also_stated_at: However, as we have limited our scope to rigid cores (which, by Theorem~\ref{thm:rigid}, does not change tractability), we will define a weighted clone $W$ to be finite-valued if its support clone is equal to $\mathbf{I}_D$, the clone of all \emph{idempotent} operations on $D$.

nodes.name: Unary constant relation
nodes.statement: For any $d\in D$, the unary constant relation $\phi_d$ is defined by $\phi_d(x)=0$ if $x=d$ and $\phi_d(x)=\infty$ otherwise.

nodes.name: Relational clone R generated by equality and constants
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{R}=\mathrm{RelClone}(\{\phi_=\}\cup\cup_{d\in D}\{\phi_d\})$.

nodes.name: Inv of idempotent operations
nodes.statement: It is known that $\mathrm{Inv}(\mathbf{I}_D)=\mathcal{R}$~\cite{Bulatov05:classifying}.
conclusions: $\mathrm{Inv}(\mathbf{I}_D)=\mathcal{R}$

nodes.name: Weighted relational clones of finite-valued weighted clones
nodes.statement: The weighted relational clones corresponding to finite-valued weighted clones are those that are subsets of the weighted relational clone generated by $\mathcal{R}$ and finite-valued weighted relations.
conclusions: are those that are subsets of the weighted relational clone generated by $\mathcal{R}$ and finite-valued weighted relations

nodes.name: Feasibility relations in finite-valued weighted clones lie in R
nodes.statement: Let $W$ be a finite-valued weighted clone on $D$. Then for any weighted relation $\phi\in\mathrm{Imp}(W)$ we have $\mathrm{Feas}(\phi)\in\mathcal{R}$.
assumptions: $W$ be a finite-valued weighted clone on $D$
conclusions: $\mathrm{Feas}(\phi)\in\mathcal{R}$

nodes.name: Finite-valued case (2a), (2b) is trivial
nodes.statement: If $W$ contains a weighting described in Theorem~\ref{thm:class2}\,(2a) then, by Proposition~\ref{prop:majority}, $\mathrm{Imp}(W)$ is crisp and thus every $\phi\in\mathrm{Imp}(W)$ can be written as the addition of a rational constant to a weighted relation in $\mathcal{R}$. Hence $\mathrm{Imp}(W)$ is tractable. Similarly, if $W$ contains a weighting described in Theorem~\ref{thm:class2}\,(2b) then, by Proposition~\ref{prop:minority}, $\mathrm{Imp}(W)$ is crisp and thus every $\phi\in\mathrm{Imp}(W)$ can be written as the addition of a rational constant to a weighted relation in $\mathcal{R}$. Hence $\mathrm{Imp}(W)$ is tractable.

nodes.name: Finite-valued (2c) weighted clones: sums of unary relations and equality
nodes.statement: Let $W$ be a finite-valued weighted clone. If $W$ contains a positive weighting described in Theorem~\ref{thm:class2}\,(2c) then every weighted relation $\phi\in\mathrm{Imp}(W)$ can be expressed as a sum of unary weighted relations and the binary equality relation $\phi_=$.
assumptions: $W$ contains a positive weighting described in Theorem~\ref{thm:class2}\,(2c)
conclusions: every weighted relation $\phi\in\mathrm{Imp}(W)$ can be expressed as a sum of unary weighted relations and the binary equality relation $\phi_=$
nodes.statement_short: In a finite-valued weighted clone with a (2c) weighting, every improved weighted relation is a sum of unary terms and equality.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 10
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we can assume the weighting assigns weight $-1$ to each of the three projections and still is as described in Theorem~\ref{thm:class2}\,(2c). An $m$-ary relation $R$ on $D$ is called trivial if $R=D^m$. First we show than any relation $R\in\mathcal{R}$ can be expressed as a sum of unary relations, trivial relations, and $\phi_=$. The claim holds true for the generators of $\mathcal{R}$, that is, for $\phi_=$ and $\phi_d$ for all $d\in D$. Next, if $R=R_1\wedge R_2$ and the claim holds true for both $R_1$ and $R_2$ the it also holds true for $R$. Finally, let $R=\exists x R'$ and assume that $R'$ satisfies the claim. If $x$ appears in some $\phi_=$ in $R'$, say $\phi_=(x,x')$, then we can replace all occurrences of $x$ by $x'$. Otherwise, $x$ appears only in constant and trivial relations in $R'$. If the conjunction of the unary relations that $x$ appears in is empty then the claim holds trivially. Otherwise, we can replace $x$ by any other variable. Consequently, for any $\phi\in\mathrm{Imp}(W)$, $\mathrm{Feas}(\phi)$ can be written as a sum of unary relations, trivial relations, and $\phi_=$. Observe that any $\phi$ with $\mathrm{Feas}(\phi)=\phi_=$ can be written as a sum of $\phi_=$ and the unary weighted relation $\phi'(x)=\phi(x,x)$. Thus, it remains to show that any $\phi\in\mathrm{Imp}(W)$ with $\mathrm{Feas}(\phi)$ being a trivial relation can be written as a sum of unary weighted relations. For any $m$-tuple $\tup{x}\in D^m$, we will write $\tup{x}[i\leftarrow d]$ to denote the tuple with $d\in D$ {substituted} at position $i$. In other words, $\tup{x}[i\leftarrow d]$ is the $m$-tuple identical to $\tup{x}$ except (possibly) at position $i$, where it is equal to $d$. We will use~\cite[Lemma~6.23]{Cohen06:complexitysoft} which says that a weighted relation $\phi:D^m\to\mbox{$\mathbb Q$}$ can be expressed as a sum of unary weighted relations if and only if, for all $\tup{x},\tup{y}\in D^m$ and all $1\leq i\leq m$, we have \begin{equation} \phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{y}) = \phi(\tup{x}[i\leftarrow \tup{y}[i]]) + \phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow \tup{x}[i]])\,. \end{equation} Take any $\tup{x},\tup{y}\in D^m$ and $1\leq i\leq m$. Let $a=\tup{x}[i]$ and $b=\tup{y}[i]$. Now consider the tuples $\tup{x}$, $\tup{x}[i\leftarrow b]$, and $\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]$. By applying the weighting from the statement of the proposition as in~\eqref{eq:WPOL}, we get $\phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{x}[i\leftarrow b])+\phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]) \geq 2\phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{y})$ and thus $\phi(\tup{x}[i\leftarrow b])+\phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]) \geq \phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{y})$. Now consider the tuples $\tup{x}$, $\tup{y}$, and $\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]$. By applying the weighting from the statement of the proposition as in~\eqref{eq:WPOL}, we get $\phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{y})+\phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]) \geq 2\phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]) + \phi(\tup{x}[i\leftarrow b])$ and thus $\phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{y}) \geq \phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]) + \phi(\tup{x}[i\leftarrow b])$.
nodes.statement_short: Structural induction shows feasibility relations decompose into unary, trivial and equality parts; then the (2c) weighting gives the exchange identity of Cohen et al. Lemma 6.23.

nodes.name: Exchange identity for sums of unary weighted relations (11)
nodes.statement: \phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{y}) = \phi(\tup{x}[i\leftarrow \tup{y}[i]]) + \phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow \tup{x}[i]])\,.

nodes.name: Symmetrise via Lemma 2; trivial relations
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we can assume the weighting assigns weight $-1$ to each of the three projections and still is as described in Theorem~\ref{thm:class2}\,(2c). An $m$-ary relation $R$ on $D$ is called trivial if $R=D^m$.
nodes.statement_short: Use Lemma 2 to normalise projection weights to $-1$; call $R$ trivial if $R=D^m$.

nodes.name: Claim: relations in R decompose
nodes.statement: First we show than any relation $R\in\mathcal{R}$ can be expressed as a sum of unary relations, trivial relations, and $\phi_=$. The claim holds true for the generators of $\mathcal{R}$, that is, for $\phi_=$ and $\phi_d$ for all $d\in D$. Next, if $R=R_1\wedge R_2$ and the claim holds true for both $R_1$ and $R_2$ the it also holds true for $R$. Finally, let $R=\exists x R'$ and assume that $R'$ satisfies the claim. If $x$ appears in some $\phi_=$ in $R'$, say $\phi_=(x,x')$, then we can replace all occurrences of $x$ by $x'$. Otherwise, $x$ appears only in constant and trivial relations in $R'$. If the conjunction of the unary relations that $x$ appears in is empty then the claim holds trivially. Otherwise, we can replace $x$ by any other variable.
nodes.statement_short: Show every relation in $\mathcal{R}$ is a sum of unary, trivial and equality relations, by structural induction.

nodes.name: Generators
nodes.statement: The claim holds true for the generators of $\mathcal{R}$, that is, for $\phi_=$ and $\phi_d$ for all $d\in D$.
nodes.statement_short: Base case: the generators $\phi_=$ and $\phi_d$.

nodes.name: Conjunction
nodes.statement: Next, if $R=R_1\wedge R_2$ and the claim holds true for both $R_1$ and $R_2$ the it also holds true for $R$.
nodes.statement_short: Inductive step for conjunction.

nodes.name: Existential quantification
nodes.statement: Finally, let $R=\exists x R'$ and assume that $R'$ satisfies the claim. If $x$ appears in some $\phi_=$ in $R'$, say $\phi_=(x,x')$, then we can replace all occurrences of $x$ by $x'$. Otherwise, $x$ appears only in constant and trivial relations in $R'$. If the conjunction of the unary relations that $x$ appears in is empty then the claim holds trivially. Otherwise, we can replace $x$ by any other variable.
nodes.statement_short: Inductive step for projection: eliminate $x$ via equality or by replacing it.

nodes.name: Reduce to trivial feasibility
nodes.statement: Consequently, for any $\phi\in\mathrm{Imp}(W)$, $\mathrm{Feas}(\phi)$ can be written as a sum of unary relations, trivial relations, and $\phi_=$. Observe that any $\phi$ with $\mathrm{Feas}(\phi)=\phi_=$ can be written as a sum of $\phi_=$ and the unary weighted relation $\phi'(x)=\phi(x,x)$. Thus, it remains to show that any $\phi\in\mathrm{Imp}(W)$ with $\mathrm{Feas}(\phi)$ being a trivial relation can be written as a sum of unary weighted relations.
nodes.statement_short: Feasibility relations decompose and equality parts are handled by $\phi'(x)=\phi(x,x)$; it remains to treat trivial feasibility relations.

nodes.name: Substitution notation
nodes.statement: For any $m$-tuple $\tup{x}\in D^m$, we will write $\tup{x}[i\leftarrow d]$ to denote the tuple with $d\in D$ {substituted} at position $i$. In other words, $\tup{x}[i\leftarrow d]$ is the $m$-tuple identical to $\tup{x}$ except (possibly) at position $i$, where it is equal to $d$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the substituted tuple $\tup{x}[i\leftarrow d]$.

nodes.name: Recall characterisation of unary sums
nodes.statement: We will use~\cite[Lemma~6.23]{Cohen06:complexitysoft} which says that a weighted relation $\phi:D^m\to\mbox{$\mathbb Q$}$ can be expressed as a sum of unary weighted relations if and only if, for all $\tup{x},\tup{y}\in D^m$ and all $1\leq i\leq m$, we have \begin{equation} \phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{y}) = \phi(\tup{x}[i\leftarrow \tup{y}[i]]) + \phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow \tup{x}[i]])\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Recall Cohen et al. Lemma 6.23: unary decomposability iff the exchange identity (11).

nodes.name: Fix tuples and coordinate
nodes.statement: Take any $\tup{x},\tup{y}\in D^m$ and $1\leq i\leq m$. Let $a=\tup{x}[i]$ and $b=\tup{y}[i]$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $\tup{x},\tup{y}$, $i$ and $a,b$.

nodes.name: First exchange inequality
nodes.statement: Now consider the tuples $\tup{x}$, $\tup{x}[i\leftarrow b]$, and $\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]$. By applying the weighting from the statement of the proposition as in~\eqref{eq:WPOL}, we get $\phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{x}[i\leftarrow b])+\phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]) \geq 2\phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{y})$ and thus $\phi(\tup{x}[i\leftarrow b])+\phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]) \geq \phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{y})$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the (2c) weighting to three tuples to get one direction of (11).

nodes.name: Second exchange inequality
nodes.statement: Now consider the tuples $\tup{x}$, $\tup{y}$, and $\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]$. By applying the weighting from the statement of the proposition as in~\eqref{eq:WPOL}, we get $\phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{y})+\phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]) \geq 2\phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]) + \phi(\tup{x}[i\leftarrow b])$ and thus $\phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{y}) \geq \phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]) + \phi(\tup{x}[i\leftarrow b])$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply it to another triple for the reverse direction, proving (11).

nodes.name: Finite-valued (2c) weighted clones are tractable
nodes.statement: A finite-valued weighted clone containing a positive weighting $\omega$ described in~Theorem~\ref{thm:class2}\,(2c) is tractable.
assumptions: A finite-valued weighted clone containing a positive weighting $\omega$ described in~Theorem~\ref{thm:class2}\,(2c)
conclusions: is tractable

nodes.name: Intractable finite-valued weighted clone with a case-(1) weighting
nodes.statement: Let $D=\{0,1,2\}$. Recall from Example~\ref{ex:TP} that a binary operation $f:D^2\to D$ is \emph{conservative} if $f(x,y)\in\{x,y\}$ for all $x,y\in D$. For any conservative binary operation $f:D^2\to D$ and any 2-element subdomain $\{a,b\}\subseteq D$, the restriction $\Crestrict{f}{\{a,b\}}$ of $f$ onto $\{a,b\}$ behaves either as $\ensuremath{e}^{(2)}_1$, $\ensuremath{e}^{(2)}_2$, $\min$, or $\max$, where $\min$ and $\max$ are the two operations that return the smaller (larger) of its two arguments with respect to the usual order $0<1<2$, respectively. Consider the operations in Table~\ref{table:w} described by their behaviour on the various 2-element subdomains. \begin{table}[htb] \begin{center} \begin{tabular}{lccc|l} $\mathbf{f}$ & \{\textbf{0},\textbf{1}\} & \{\textbf{0},\textbf{2}\} & \{\textbf{1},\textbf{2}\} & $\mathbf{\omega(f)}$\\ \hline $f_1$ & $\ensuremath{e}^{(2)}_1$ & $\ensuremath{e}^{(2)}_1$ & $\ensuremath{e}^{(2)}_1$ & -0.5 \\ $f_2$ & $\ensuremath{e}^{(2)}_2$ & $\ensuremath{e}^{(2)}_2$ & $\ensuremath{e}^{(2)}_2$ & -0.5 \\ $f_3$ & $\ensuremath{e}^{(2)}_1$ & $\min$ & $\ensuremath{e}^{(2)}_1$ & 0.5 \\ $f_4$ & $\ensuremath{e}^{(2)}_2$ & $\min$ & $\ensuremath{e}^{(2)}_2$ & 0.5 \\ \end{tabular} \end{center} \caption{Definition of $\omega$} \end{table} Note that $f_1=\ensuremath{e}^{(2)}_1$ and $f_{2}=\ensuremath{e}^{(2)}_2$. The weighting $\omega$ is defined by the last column of Table~\ref{table:w}. Note that $\omega$ is not commutative. It can be checked that $\omega$ is a weighted polymorphism of the finite-valued weighted relation $\phi : \{0,1,2\} \to \mbox{$\mathbb Q$}$ defined in Table~\ref{table:phi}. \begin{table}[hbt] \begin{center} \begin{tabular}{c|ccc} $\phi$ & \textbf{0} & \textbf{1} & \textbf{2} \\ \hline \textbf{0} & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ \textbf{1} & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ \textbf{2} & 1 & 1 & 1 \end{tabular} \end{center} \caption{Definition of $\phi$} \end{table} Now since $\mathrm{argmin} \phi=\{(0,1),(1,0)\}$, we have that $\phi$ satisfies the (MC) condition~\cite{tz13:stoc} and thus can be used to reduce from Max-Cut~\cite{Cohen06:complexitysoft}. Thus, $W=\mathrm{wClone}(\{\omega\})$ is intractable.
nodes.statement_short: A non-commutative binary weighting of conservative operations on $\{0,1,2\}$ improves a Max-Cut-like $\phi$, so wClone($\omega$) is intractable.

nodes.name: Case (1) gives tractable and intractable finite-valued clones
nodes.statement: Thus weightings described in Theorem~\ref{thm:class2}\,(1) can lead to both tractable and intractable finite-valued weighted clones.
conclusions: weightings described in Theorem~\ref{thm:class2}\,(1) can lead to both tractable and intractable finite-valued weighted clones

nodes.name: Finite-valued dichotomy: binary commutative weighting
nodes.statement: The authors have recently shown that with respect to tractability of finite-valued constraint languages the necessary and sufficient condition is having a binary weighting $\omega$ that assigns positive weight to idempotent \emph{commutative} operations only; that is, for every $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ we have $f(x,y)=f(y,x)$ for all $x,y\in D$~\cite{tz13:stoc}.\footnote{The result from~\cite{tz13:stoc} extends from finite-valued constraint languages to finite-valued weighted relational clones as adding the binary equality relation and unary constant relations does not affect tractability in the presence of a binary commutative weighted polymorphism.}
conclusions: with respect to tractability of finite-valued constraint languages the necessary and sufficient condition is having a binary weighting $\omega$ that assigns positive weight to idempotent \emph{commutative} operations only

nodes.name: Interplay of cases (1) and (3) in finite-valued clones
nodes.statement: However, the precise interplay of case~(1) and case~(3) of Theorem~\ref{thm:class2} is currently unknown.

nodes.name: Full weighted relational clone is NP-hard
nodes.statement: Any weighted relational clone $\Gamma\subseteq{\bf \Phi}_D$ with $\mathrm{wRelClone}(\Gamma)={\bf \Phi}_D$ is NP-hard.
conclusions: is NP-hard

nodes.name: Maximal weighted relational clone
nodes.statement: A weighted relational clone $\Gamma\subseteq{\bf \Phi}_D$ is called \emph{maximal} if $\mathrm{wRelClone}(\Gamma)\neq{\bf \Phi}_D$ but for any $\phi\not\in\Gamma$ we have $\mathrm{wRelClone}(\Gamma\cup\{\phi\})={\bf \Phi}_D$.
also_stated_at: A weighted relational clone on $D$ is called \emph{maximal} if it is as large as possible but $\mathrm{wRelClone}(\Gamma)\neq{\bf \Phi}_D$.
nodes.label: def:maximal

nodes.name: Maximal language iff maximal weighted relational clone
nodes.statement: It follows that a valued constraint language $\Gamma$ is maximal if and only if the weighted relational clone $\mathrm{wRelClone}(\Gamma)$ is maximal.
conclusions: a valued constraint language $\Gamma$ is maximal if and only if the weighted relational clone $\mathrm{wRelClone}(\Gamma)$ is maximal
equivalent_conditions: a valued constraint language $\Gamma$ is maximal
the weighted relational clone $\mathrm{wRelClone}(\Gamma)$ is maximal

nodes.name: Maximal relational clone
nodes.statement: As a special case of Definition~\ref{def:maximal}, we get that a relational clone $\Gamma$ is maximal if $\Gamma\neq{\bf R}_D$ but for any $R\in{\bf R}_D$ we have $\mathrm{RelClone}(\Gamma\cup\{R\})={\bf R}_D$.

nodes.name: Minimal weighted clone
nodes.statement: A weighted clone $W$ with support clone $C$ is called \emph{minimal} if $W\neq{\bf W}_C^0$ and every positive weighting $\omega\in W$ satisfies $\mathrm{wClone}(\omega)=W$.
also_stated_at: A weighted clone is called \emph{minimal} if it is not zero-valued but the only weighted clone properly included in it is the zero-valued weighted clone.

nodes.name: Maximal weighted relational clones correspond to minimal weighted clones
nodes.statement: Maximal weighted relational clones correspond, via the Galois correspondence given in Theorem~\ref{thm:wgc}, to minimal weighted clones.
conclusions: Maximal weighted relational clones correspond, via the Galois correspondence given in Theorem~\ref{thm:wgc}, to minimal weighted clones

nodes.name: Maximal non-crisp weighted relational clones are intractable
nodes.statement: All maximal non-crisp weighted relational clones are intractable.
conclusions: are intractable

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 11
nodes.statement: If $\Gamma$ contains all finite-valued weighted relations then it is intractable. Otherwise, there is a finite-valued weighted relation $\phi\not\in\Gamma$. Since $\phi$ is finite-valued we have $\mathrm{Feas}(\Gamma)=\mathrm{Feas}(\mathrm{wRelClone}(\Gamma\cup\{\phi\}))$. But then either $\mathrm{Feas}(\Gamma)=\mathbf{R}_D$, in which case $\Gamma$ is intractable, or $\mathrm{Feas}(\Gamma)=\mathrm{Feas}(\mathrm{wRelClone}(\Gamma\cup\{\phi\}))\neq\mathbf{R}_D$, in which case $\Gamma$ is not maximal.
nodes.statement_short: Either $\Gamma$ has all finite-valued relations (intractable), or adding a finite-valued $\phi$ keeps Feas fixed, forcing intractability or non-maximality.

nodes.name: All finite-valued relations present
nodes.statement: If $\Gamma$ contains all finite-valued weighted relations then it is intractable.
nodes.statement_short: If $\Gamma$ contains every finite-valued weighted relation it is intractable.

nodes.name: Some finite-valued relation missing
nodes.statement: Otherwise, there is a finite-valued weighted relation $\phi\not\in\Gamma$. Since $\phi$ is finite-valued we have $\mathrm{Feas}(\Gamma)=\mathrm{Feas}(\mathrm{wRelClone}(\Gamma\cup\{\phi\}))$. But then either $\mathrm{Feas}(\Gamma)=\mathbf{R}_D$, in which case $\Gamma$ is intractable, or $\mathrm{Feas}(\Gamma)=\mathrm{Feas}(\mathrm{wRelClone}(\Gamma\cup\{\phi\}))\neq\mathbf{R}_D$, in which case $\Gamma$ is not maximal.
nodes.statement_short: Adding a missing finite-valued $\phi$ preserves Feas; then $\Gamma$ is intractable or not maximal.

nodes.name: Gordan's Theorem
nodes.statement: Let $A\in\mathbb{Q}^{n\times m}$ be a matrix. Either $Ax=0$, where $x\in\mathbb{Q}^{m}$ with $x\geq 0$ and $x\neq 0$, or $\exists y\in\mathbb{Q}^n$ with $y^{\intercal}A>0$.
conclusions: Either $Ax=0$, where $x\in\mathbb{Q}^{m}$ with $x\geq 0$ and $x\neq 0$, or $\exists y\in\mathbb{Q}^n$ with $y^{\intercal}A>0$
nodes.statement_short: Theorem of the alternative: either $Ax=0$ has a nonzero nonnegative solution or some $y$ has $y^T A>0$.
nodes.label: thm:gordan

nodes.name: Improper superpositions can be made proper
nodes.statement: By Definition~\ref{defn:wclone}, only \emph{proper} superpositions are allowed within a weighted clone. However, the following result from~\cite{cccjz13:sicomp} shows that any weighted sum of arbitrary superpositions of a pair of weightings $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ can be obtained by taking a weighted sum of superpositions of $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ with projection operations, and then taking a superposition of the result. Given that superpositions with projections are always proper~\cite{cccjz13:sicomp}, this result implies that any weighting which can be expressed as a weighted sum of arbitrary (i.e., possibly improper) superpositions can also be expressed as a superposition of a weighted sum of \emph{proper} superpositions.
nodes.statement_short: Any weighted sum of possibly improper superpositions equals a superposition of a weighted sum of proper ones (via Lemma 3).

nodes.name: Sum of superpositions lemma
nodes.statement: Let $C$ be a clone, and let $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ be weightings of $C$, of arity $k$ and $\ell$ respectively. For any $g_1,\ldots,g_k \in C^{(m)}$ and any $g'_1,\ldots,g'_\ell \in C^{(m)}$, \begin{equation*} c_1 \, \omega_1[g_1,\ldots,g_k] + \ c_2 \, \omega_2[g'_1,\ldots,g'_{\ell}] = \omega[g_1,\ldots,g_k,g'_1,\ldots,g'_{\ell}]\,, \end{equation*} where $\omega = c_1 \, \omega_1[e^{(k+\ell)}_1,\ldots,e^{(k+\ell)}_k] + \ c_2 \, \omega_2[e^{(k+\ell)}_{k+1},\ldots,e^{(k+\ell)}_{k+\ell}]$
assumptions: $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ be weightings of $C$, of arity $k$ and $\ell$ respectively
nodes.statement_short: A weighted sum of two superposed weightings equals one superposition of a weighting built from superpositions with projections.
nodes.label: lemma:sumofsuperpos

nodes.name: Pixley operations of type 1, 2, 3
nodes.statement: We call (ternary) operations corresponding to columns 5, 6, and 7 in Table~\ref{tab:sharp3} Pixley operations of type 1, 2, and 3 respectively, and will denote by P1 (P2 and P3) the Pixley operations of type 1 (2 and 3, respectively).

nodes.name: Semiprojections of type 1, 2, 3
nodes.statement: We call (ternary) semiprojections corresponding to columns 2, 3, and 4 in Table~\ref{tab:sharp3} semiprojections of type 1, 2, and 3 respectively, and will denote by S1 (S2 and S3) the semiprojections of type 1 (2 and 3, respectively).

nodes.name: Type of a k-ary semiprojection
nodes.statement: More generally, a $k$-ary semiprojection $f$ is called of type $1\leq i\leq k$ if equating any two inputs of $f$ results in $\ensuremath{e}^{(k)}_i$.

nodes.name: Cyclic permutation changes Pixley type
nodes.statement: For any Pixley operation $f$ of type $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ we can obtain, by (cyclically) permuting the arguments of $f$, Pixley operations of the other two types.
conclusions: we can obtain, by (cyclically) permuting the arguments of $f$, Pixley operations of the other two types

nodes.name: Related Pixley operations
nodes.statement: Two Pixley operations $f$ and $g$ of different types are called \emph{related} if there is a permutation $\pi\in\mathrm{Cycl}_3$ such that $f=g^\pi$.

nodes.name: Related semiprojections
nodes.statement: Similarly, two semiprojections $f$ and $g$ of different types are called related if there is a permutation $\pi\in\mathrm{Cycl}_3$ such that $f=g^\pi$.

nodes.name: Types of sharp operations under cyclic permutation (Table 3)
nodes.statement: The following table, which can be verified using the definitions above, will be useful in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:class2}. It lists the types of ternary sharp operations obtained by superposing a ternary sharp operation of an arbitrary type (columns in Table~\ref{tab:types}) with any of the three cyclic permutations of the three ternary projections (rows in Table~\ref{tab:types}).
conclusions: It lists the types of ternary sharp operations obtained by superposing a ternary sharp operation of an arbitrary type (columns in Table~\ref{tab:types}) with any of the three cyclic permutations of the three ternary projections (rows in Table~\ref{tab:types})

nodes.name: Permuted semiprojection and Pixley types can differ
nodes.statement: Note that taking a semiprojection $f$ of type $i$ and a Pixley operation $g$ of type $i$, $f^\pi$ and $g^\pi$ can be of different types; e.g., if $f$ is a semiprojection of type $1$ and $g$ is a Pixley operation of type $1$ and $\pi=(2,3,1)$ then $f^\pi$ is a semiprojection of type $2$ and $g^\pi$ is a Pixley operation of type $3$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5 (Main theorem)
nodes.statement: It suffices to consider the ternary case as the rest of the theorem follows from (the proof of) Theorem~\ref{thm:class1} and the fact that $W$ is a rigid core, which eliminates the first case of Theorem~\ref{thm:class1}. Let $W$ be a weighted clone containing a ternary positive weighting $\omega$ such that every $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ is sharp. (If some $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ were not sharp then we could show, as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:class1}, that the case~(1) holds.) We denote by $C$ the support clone of $W$. We assume that none of the cases (2a), (2b), (2c), (3) (with $k=3$) of the theorem applies as we would be done in any of these cases. By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we can assume that $\omega$ assigns weight $-1$ to each of the three ternary projections and thus \begin{equation} \sum_{f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)}\omega(f)\ =\ 3\,. \end{equation} Let $P_i\subseteq C$ be the Pixley operations of type $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ from $C$. Since $C$ is a clone we have \begin{equation} |P_1|\ =\ |P_2|\ =\ |P_3|\,. \end{equation} By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we have for any three related Pixley operations $p_1\in P_1$, $p_2\in P_2$, and $p_3\in P_3$, \begin{equation} \omega(p_1)\ =\ \omega(p_2)\ =\ \omega(p_3)\,, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \sum_{p\in P_1} \omega(p)\ =\ \sum_{p\in P_2} \omega(p)\ =\ \sum_{p\in P_3} \omega(p)\,. \end{equation} We set $P=P_1\cup P_2\cup P_3$ to be the set of all Pixley operations from $C$ and $w(P)=\sum_{p\in P}\omega(p)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, the same holds for the three types of ternary semiprojections. In particular, we denote by $S_i\subseteq C$ the operations from $C$ that are semiprojections of type $i\in\{1,2,3\}$. Since $C$ is a clone, we have \begin{equation} |S_1|\ =\ |S_2|\ =\ |S_3|\,. \end{equation} For any three related semiprojections $s_1\in S_1$, $s_2\in S_2$, and $s_3\in S_3$, \begin{equation} \omega(s_1)\ =\ \omega(s_2)\ =\ \omega(s_3)\,, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \sum_{s\in S_1} \omega(s)\ =\ \sum_{s\in S_2} \omega(s)\ =\ \sum_{s\in S_3} \omega(s)\,. \end{equation} We set $S=S_1\cup S_2\cup S_3$ to be the set of all semiprojections from $C$ and $w(S)=\sum_{s\in S}\omega(s)$. To simplify the presentation, we use the same notation for weightings, index sets, etc. in the following three steps since the steps are similar (but independent). Thus, for example, when one reads $J$ in Step II it refers to $J$ defined in Step II and not in Step I. \textbf{Step I}: Eliminating Pixley operations. We now show how to eliminate Pixley operations if needed, that is, assume $w(P)>0$ and thus some operations from $P$ are assigned positive weight. First assume that $\omega$ assigns positive weight to only Pixley operations, that is, ${\rm supp}(\omega)\subseteq P$. Hence $w(P)=3$. Take arbitrary $p_1,p'_1\in P_1$, $p_2,p'_2\in P_2$, and $p_3,p'_3\in P_3$. The following claims can be verified from the definitions: $p_1[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p'_1]$ is a majority operation, $p_2[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p'_1]=\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1$, and $p_3[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p'_1]=\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2$. Consequently, $\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p'_1]$ assigns weight $-1$ to $p'_1$, $+1$ to majority operations, and $0$ otherwise. Similarly, $\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,p'_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3]$ assigns weight $-1$ to $p'_2$, $+1$ to majority operations, and $0$ otherwise. Finally, $\omega[p'_3,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3]$ assigns weight $-1$ to $p'_3$, $+1$ to majority operations, and $0$ otherwise. Overall, the weighting \begin{equation} \mu\ =\ \omega+\sum_{p\in P_1}\omega(p)\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p] +\sum_{p\in P_2}\omega(p)\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,p,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3] +\sum_{p\in P_3}\omega(p)\omega[p,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3] \end{equation} assigns weight $-1$ to each of the three ternary projections and weight $3$ to majority operations. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}, the intermediate superpositions in~\eqref{eq:pixleyonly} can be improper as long as the resulting weighting $\mu$ is indeed a weighting. Thus $\mu\in W$ and case~(2a) of the theorem holds. Let assume that ${\rm supp}(\omega)\not\subseteq P$, that is, $\omega$ assigns positive weight not only to Pixley operations. Let $J=\{(p_1,p_2,p_3)\in P_1\times P_2\times P_3\:|\:\mbox{$p_1, p_2, p_3$ are related}\}$ and $\bar{J}=\{(\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3)\}\cup J$. We consider the following linear system: for all Pixley operations $p\in P$, \begin{equation} \sum_{(f,g,h) \in \bar{J}}x_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h](p)\ =\ 0\,. \end{equation} By Gordan's Theorem,~\eqref{eq:pixleyzero} has a nonzero nonnegative solution if and only if the following system of strict inequalities is unsatisfiable: for all $(f,g,h) \in \bar{J}$, \begin{equation} \sum_{p \in P}y_p\omega[f,g,h](p)\ >\ 0\,. \end{equation} Consider the case $\tuple{f,g,h}=\tuple{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}$. Then $\omega[f,g,h]=\omega$ and thus $\omega[f,g,h](p)=\omega(p)>0$ for all $p\in {\rm supp}(\omega)\cap P$, by the definition of $P$. Moreover, by~\eqref{eq:Pweights} \begin{equation} \sum_{p\in P}y_p\omega(p) \ =\ \sum_{p_1\in P_1}(y_{p_1}+y_{p_2}+y_{p_3})\omega(p_1)\,, \end{equation} where we denoted (with a slight abuse of notation) by $p_2$ and $p_3$ the related operations of $p_1$. For $\tuple{f,g,h} = \tuple{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}$ the LHS of~\eqref{eq:pixleygordan} is equal to~\eqref{eq:split}. Thus, for~\eqref{eq:pixleygordan} to hold in this case we must have at least one triple of related operations $\tuple{p_1,p_2,p_3} \in J$ with $y_{p_1} + y_{p_2} + y_{p_3} > 0$. Suppose $\tuple{p_1,p_2,p_3}\in J$ is chosen to maximise $y_{p_1} + y_{p_2} + y_{p_3}$. The left-hand side of \eqref{eq:pixleygordan} when $\tuple{f,g,h} = \tuple{p_1,p_2,p_3}$ is equal to \begin{equation} - y_{p_1} - y_{p_2} - y_{p_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s)\,, \end{equation} since $o[p_1,p_2,p_3]$ is equal to a Pixley operation only when $o$ is one of the three projections, which give the first three terms in~\eqref{eq:abc}, or a semiprojection, which gives the last term of~\eqref{eq:abc}, the sum over $S$. We have \begin{equation} \begin{split} \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s)\ =\ & \sum_{s_1\in S_1}y_{s_1[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s_1) + \sum_{s_2\in S_2}y_{s_2[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s_2) + \sum_{s_3\in S_3}y_{s_3[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s_3) \\ =\ & \sum_{\substack{\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}\in S_1\times S_2\times S_3\\s_1,s_2,s_3\mbox{ \scriptsize related}}}(y_{s_1[p_1,p_2,p_3]}+y_{s_2[p_1,p_2,p_3]}+y_{s_3[p_1,p_2,p_3]})\omega(s_1) \\ \leq\ & \frac{\omega(S)}{3}(y_{p_1}+y_{p_2}+y_{p_3}),\\ \end{split} \end{equation} where the first equality follows from the definition of $S$; the second equality follows from fact that $s[p_1,p_2,p_3]$ is a Pixley operation of type $i$ given $s$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, where $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, and hence $\tuple{s_1[p_1,p_2,p_3],s_2[p_1,p_2,p_3],s_3[p_1,p_2,p_3]}$ is a triple of related Pixley operations given that $\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}$ is a triple of related semiprojections; and the last inequality follows from the definition of $w(S)$ and the choice of $(p_1,p_2,p_3)$. Combining~\eqref{eq:abc} and~\eqref{eq:S3}, we have \begin{equation} - y_{p_1} - y_{p_2} - y_{p_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s) \ \leq\ - y_{p_1} - y_{p_2} - y_{p_3} + \frac{w(S)}{3}(y_{p_1}+y_{p_2}+y_{p_3}) \ <\ 0\,, \end{equation} where the last strict inequality follows from $w(S)<3$ since $w(P)>0$ and~\eqref{eq:sum3}. Hence, \eqref{eq:pixleygordan} is unsatisfiable and, by Gordan's Theorem, \eqref{eq:pixleyzero} must have a nonzero nonnegative solution $x^*$. We finish Step~I by using $x^*$ to prove the existence of a weighting in $W$ that assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations. Let \begin{equation} \mu'=\sum_{(f,g,h) \in \bar{J}}x^*_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h]\,, \end{equation} be a weighted sum of superpositions of $\omega$. By the choice of $x^*$, $\mu'$ assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations. From the definition of $\bar{J}$, \begin{equation} \mu'\ =\ x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3]+\sum_{(f,g,h)\in J}x^*_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h]\,. \end{equation} We know that $x^*$ is nonzero and nonnegative. Note that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}=0$ for all $(f,g,h)\in J$ would contradict that $\mu'$ assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations. Let $(f,g,h)\in J$ and $i\in\{1,2,3\}$. Then $o[f,g,h]$ is a Pixley operation of type $i$ if $o$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, $o[f,g,h]$ is a semiprojection of type $i$ if $o$ is a Pixley operation of type $i$, $o[f,g,h]$ is a majority operation if $o$ is a minority operation, and finally $o[f,g,h]$ is a minority operation if $o$ is a majority operation. It follows that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}=0$ would contradict that $\mu'$ assigns zero weight all Pixley operations since Pixley operations of type $i$ would be assigned negative weight since $w(S)-3<0$ as $w(P)>0$. Thus $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}>0$ for at least one $(f,g,h)\in J$. Consequently, $\mu'$ is a nonzero weighting that assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}, $\mu'\in W$. \textbf{Step II}: Eliminating semiprojections. We now show how to eliminate semiprojections if needed. If $\mu'$ obtained in Step I assigns positive weight to only semiprojections then we are in case (3) (with $k$=3) of the theorem. Thus let assume that $\mu'$ assigns positive weight to semiprojections and at least one majority or minority operation. By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we can assume the existence of a ternary weighting $\omega\in W$ which assigns weight -1 to all three projections (and thus assigns total positive weight 3). We will use the same notation for $S$, $S_1$, $S_2$, and $S_3$ as before although note that the weighting $\omega$ is now different from the one we had before and throughout Step I. We have $w(S)<3$ and~\eqref{eq:Srelated},~\eqref{eq:Scard},~\eqref{eq:Sweights} still hold for $\omega$. We again use Gordan's Theorem to show that there exists a nonzero ternary weighting in $W$ that assigns positive weight to majority and minority operations only. Let $J=\{(s_1,s_2,s_3)\in S_1\times S_2\times S_3\:|\:\mbox{$s_1, s_2, s_3$ are related}\}$ and $\bar{J}=\{(\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3)\}\cup J$. We consider the following linear system: for all semiprojections $s\in S$, \begin{equation} \sum_{\tuple{f,g,h}\in \bar{J}}x_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h](s)\ =\ 0\,. \end{equation} By Gordan's Theorem,~\eqref{eq:semiprojzero} has a nonzero nonnegative solution if and only if the following system of strict inequalities is unsatisfiable: for all $(f,g,h) \in \bar{J}$, \begin{equation} \sum_{s \in S}y_s\omega[f,g,h](s)\ >\ 0\,. \end{equation} As in Step I, we can argue that~\eqref{eq:semiprojgordan} is unsatisfiable. Consider the case $\tuple{f,g,h}=\tuple{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}$. Then $\omega[f,g,h]=\omega$ and thus $\omega[f,g,h](s)=\omega(s)>0$ for all $s\in{\rm supp}(\omega)\cap S$, by the definition of $S$. Moreover, by~\eqref{eq:Sweights} \begin{equation} \sum_{s\in S}\omega(s)y_s \ =\ \sum_{s_1\in S_1}(y_{s_1}+y_{s_2}+y_{s_3})\omega(s_1)\,, \end{equation} where we denoted by $s_2$ and $s_3$ the related operations of $s_1$. Therefore, for \eqref{eq:semiprojgordan} to hold when $\tuple{f,g,h} = \tuple{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}$ we must have at least one triple of related semiprojections $\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3} \in J$ with $y_{s_1} + y_{s_2} + y_{s_3} > 0$. Suppose $\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}\in J$ is chosen to maximise $y_{s_1} + y_{s_2} + y_{s_3}$. The left-hand side of \eqref{eq:semiprojgordan} when $\tuple{f,g,h} = \tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}$ is equal to \begin{equation} - y_{s_1} - y_{s_2} - y_{s_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s)\,, \end{equation} since $o[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is equal to a semiprojection only when $o$ is one of the three projections, which give the first three terms in~\eqref{eq:Sabc}, or a semiprojection, which gives the last term of~\eqref{eq:Sabc}, the sum over $S$. We have \begin{equation} \begin{split} \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s)\ =\ & \sum_{s_1\in S_1}y_{s_1[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s_1) + \sum_{s_2\in S_2}y_{s_2[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s_2) + \sum_{s_3\in S_3}y_{s_3[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s_3) \\ =\ & \sum_{\substack{\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}\in S_1\times S_2\times S_3\\s_1,s_2,s_3\mbox{\scriptsize related}}}(y_{s_1[s_1,s_2,s_3]}+y_{s_2[s_1,s_2,s_3]}+y_{s_3[s_1,s_2,s_3]})\omega(s_1) \\ \leq\ & \frac{\omega(S)}{3}(y_{s_1}+y_{s_2}+y_{s_3}),\\ \end{split} \end{equation} where the first equality follows from the definition of $S$; the second equality follows from fact that $s[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is a semiprojection of type $i$ given $s$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, where $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, and hence $\tuple{s_1[s_1,s_2,s_3],s_2[s_1,s_2,s_3],s_3[s_1,s_2,s_3]}$ is a triple of related semiprojections given that $\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}$ is a triple of related semiprojections; and the last inequality follows from the definition of $w(S)$ and the choice of $(s_1,s_2,s_3)$. Combining~\eqref{eq:Sabc} and~\eqref{eq:SS3}, we have \begin{equation} - y_{s_1} - y_{s_2} - y_{s_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s) \ \leq\ - y_{s_1} - y_{s_2} - y_{s_3} + \frac{w(S)}{3}(y_{s_1}+y_{s_2}+y_{s_3}) \ <\ 0\,, \end{equation} where the last strict inequality follows from $w(S)<3$. Hence, \eqref{eq:semiprojgordan} is unsatisfiable and, by Gordan's Theorem, \eqref{eq:semiprojzero} must have a nonzero nonnegative solution $x^*$. We finish Step~II by using $x^*$ to prove the existence of a weighting in $W$ that assigns zero weight to all semiprojections. Let \begin{equation} \mu=\sum_{(f,g,h) \in J}\omega[f,g,h]x^*_{f,g,h}\,, \end{equation} be a weighted sum of superpositions of $\omega$. By the choice of $x^*$, $\mu$ assigns zero weight to all semiprojections. From the definition of $\bar{J}$, \begin{equation} \mu\ =\ x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3]+\sum_{(f,g,h) \in J}x^*_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h]\,. \end{equation} We know that $x^*$ is nonzero and nonnegative. Note that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}=0$ for all $(f,g,h)\in J$ would contradict that $\mu'$ assigns zero weight to all semiprojections. Let $(s_1,s_2,s_3)\in J$ and $i\in\{1,2,3\}$. Then $o[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is a semiprojection of type $i$ if $o$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, $o[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is a majority operation if $o$ is a majority operation, and finally $o[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is a minority operation if $o$ is a minority operation. (Note that we do not need to consider the case when $f$ is a Pixley operation as $\omega$ assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations.) It follows that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}=0$ would contradict that $\mu$ assigns zero weight all semiprojections since semiprojections of type $i$ would be assigned negative weight since $w(S)-3<0$ as $\omega$ assigns positive weight to some majority or minority (or possibly both) operations. Thus $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}$ for at least one $(f,g,h)\in J$. Consequently, $\mu$ is a nonzero weighting that assigns zero weight to all semiprojections. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}, $\mu\in W$. \textbf{Step III}: Majority and minority operations. In Steps I and II, we have shown that any weighted clone $W$ with a positive ternary weighting contains a ternary weighting that assigns nonzero weight to semiprojections alone (case~(3) of the theorem with $k=3$), or a mix of majority and minority operations. Finally, we will show that if $W$ contains a weighting $\omega$ that assigns weight to majority and minority operations alone then $W$ also contains a weighting of one of the three types described in cases~(2a),~(2b), and~(2c) of the theorem. Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ denote the sets of majority and minority operations in the support of $\omega$. Suppose that $\omega$ assigns total weight $2+a$ to $M_1$ and total weight $1-a$ to $M_2$ for some $a > 0$. For each $f \in M_2$, we define $\mu_f = \omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,f]$, so $\mu_f$ assigns weight $a$ to $\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1$ and weight $-a$ to $f$. Note that $\mu_f$ is not a proper weighting, since $a > 0$. We obtain a weighting $\mu \in W$ which assigns positive weight to majority operations only as follows: \begin{equation} \mu = \omega + \sum_{f \in M_2}\frac{\omega(f)}{a}\mu_f\,. \end{equation} Similarly, suppose that $\omega$ assigns total weight $2-a$ to $M_1$ and total weight $1+a$ to $M_2$ for some $a>0$. For each $f\in M_1$, we define $\mu_f=\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,f,f]$, so $\mu_f$ assigns weight $a$ to $\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1$ and weight $-a$ to $f$. We obtain a weighting $\mu \in W$ which assigns positive weight to minority operations only as follows: \begin{equation} \mu = \omega + \sum_{f \in M_1}\frac{\omega(f)}{a}\mu_f\,. \end{equation} In both cases $\mu\in W$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to ternary sharp weightings, then eliminate Pixley operations and then semiprojections by Gordan-duality arguments, and finally rebalance majority/minority weight. The key step: the dual Gordan system is infeasible because semiprojection weight $w(S)<3$.

nodes.name: Setup: ternary sharp weighting and symmetry
nodes.statement: It suffices to consider the ternary case as the rest of the theorem follows from (the proof of) Theorem~\ref{thm:class1} and the fact that $W$ is a rigid core, which eliminates the first case of Theorem~\ref{thm:class1}. Let $W$ be a weighted clone containing a ternary positive weighting $\omega$ such that every $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ is sharp. (If some $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ were not sharp then we could show, as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:class1}, that the case~(1) holds.) We denote by $C$ the support clone of $W$. We assume that none of the cases (2a), (2b), (2c), (3) (with $k=3$) of the theorem applies as we would be done in any of these cases. By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we can assume that $\omega$ assigns weight $-1$ to each of the three ternary projections and thus \begin{equation} \sum_{f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)}\omega(f)\ =\ 3\,. \end{equation} Let $P_i\subseteq C$ be the Pixley operations of type $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ from $C$. Since $C$ is a clone we have \begin{equation} |P_1|\ =\ |P_2|\ =\ |P_3|\,. \end{equation} By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we have for any three related Pixley operations $p_1\in P_1$, $p_2\in P_2$, and $p_3\in P_3$, \begin{equation} \omega(p_1)\ =\ \omega(p_2)\ =\ \omega(p_3)\,, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \sum_{p\in P_1} \omega(p)\ =\ \sum_{p\in P_2} \omega(p)\ =\ \sum_{p\in P_3} \omega(p)\,. \end{equation} We set $P=P_1\cup P_2\cup P_3$ to be the set of all Pixley operations from $C$ and $w(P)=\sum_{p\in P}\omega(p)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, the same holds for the three types of ternary semiprojections. In particular, we denote by $S_i\subseteq C$ the operations from $C$ that are semiprojections of type $i\in\{1,2,3\}$. Since $C$ is a clone, we have \begin{equation} |S_1|\ =\ |S_2|\ =\ |S_3|\,. \end{equation} For any three related semiprojections $s_1\in S_1$, $s_2\in S_2$, and $s_3\in S_3$, \begin{equation} \omega(s_1)\ =\ \omega(s_2)\ =\ \omega(s_3)\,, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \sum_{s\in S_1} \omega(s)\ =\ \sum_{s\in S_2} \omega(s)\ =\ \sum_{s\in S_3} \omega(s)\,. \end{equation} We set $S=S_1\cup S_2\cup S_3$ to be the set of all semiprojections from $C$ and $w(S)=\sum_{s\in S}\omega(s)$. To simplify the presentation, we use the same notation for weightings, index sets, etc. in the following three steps since the steps are similar (but independent). Thus, for example, when one reads $J$ in Step II it refers to $J$ defined in Step II and not in Step I.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a symmetrised ternary sharp weighting and set up Pixley/semiprojection weight classes.

nodes.name: Reduce to ternary case
nodes.statement: It suffices to consider the ternary case as the rest of the theorem follows from (the proof of) Theorem~\ref{thm:class1} and the fact that $W$ is a rigid core, which eliminates the first case of Theorem~\ref{thm:class1}.
nodes.statement_short: Non-ternary cases follow from Theorem 4 and the rigid core assumption.

nodes.name: Ternary sharp weighting
nodes.statement: Let $W$ be a weighted clone containing a ternary positive weighting $\omega$ such that every $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ is sharp. (If some $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ were not sharp then we could show, as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:class1}, that the case~(1) holds.) We denote by $C$ the support clone of $W$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a positive ternary weighting supported on sharp operations; $C$ the support clone.

nodes.name: Assume no target case holds
nodes.statement: We assume that none of the cases (2a), (2b), (2c), (3) (with $k=3$) of the theorem applies as we would be done in any of these cases.
nodes.statement_short: Assume none of cases (2a)-(2c), (3) with $k=3$ holds.

nodes.name: Normalise via Lemma 2
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we can assume that $\omega$ assigns weight $-1$ to each of the three ternary projections and thus \begin{equation} \sum_{f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)}\omega(f)\ =\ 3\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 2, projections get weight $-1$, positive weight totals 3.

nodes.name: Pixley classes

nodes.name: Pixley weights equal across types

nodes.statement_short: Related Pixley operations have equal weight; define $P$ and $w(P)$.

nodes.name: Semiprojection weights equal across types
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, the same holds for the three types of ternary semiprojections. nodes.name: Step I: eliminating Pixley operations
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step I}: Eliminating Pixley operations. We now show how to eliminate Pixley operations if needed, that is, assume $w(P)>0$ and thus some operations from $P$ are assigned positive weight. First assume that $\omega$ assigns positive weight to only Pixley operations, that is, ${\rm supp}(\omega)\subseteq P$. Hence $w(P)=3$. Take arbitrary $p_1,p'_1\in P_1$, $p_2,p'_2\in P_2$, and $p_3,p'_3\in P_3$. The following claims can be verified from the definitions: $p_1[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p'_1]$ is a majority operation, $p_2[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p'_1]=\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1$, and $p_3[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p'_1]=\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2$. Consequently, $\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p'_1]$ assigns weight $-1$ to $p'_1$, $+1$ to majority operations, and $0$ otherwise. Similarly, $\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,p'_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3]$ assigns weight $-1$ to $p'_2$, $+1$ to majority operations, and $0$ otherwise. Finally, $\omega[p'_3,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3]$ assigns weight $-1$ to $p'_3$, $+1$ to majority operations, and $0$ otherwise. Overall, the weighting \begin{equation} \mu\ =\ \omega+\sum_{p\in P_1}\omega(p)\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p] +\sum_{p\in P_2}\omega(p)\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,p,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3] +\sum_{p\in P_3}\omega(p)\omega[p,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3] \end{equation} assigns weight $-1$ to each of the three ternary projections and weight $3$ to majority operations. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}, the intermediate superpositions in~\eqref{eq:pixleyonly} can be improper as long as the resulting weighting $\mu$ is indeed a weighting. Thus $\mu\in W$ and case~(2a) of the theorem holds. Let assume that ${\rm supp}(\omega)\not\subseteq P$, that is, $\omega$ assigns positive weight not only to Pixley operations. Let $J=\{(p_1,p_2,p_3)\in P_1\times P_2\times P_3\:|\:\mbox{$p_1, p_2, p_3$ are related}\}$ and $\bar{J}=\{(\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3)\}\cup J$. We consider the following linear system: for all Pixley operations $p\in P$, \begin{equation} \sum_{(f,g,h) \in \bar{J}}x_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h](p)\ =\ 0\,. \end{equation} By Gordan's Theorem,~\eqref{eq:pixleyzero} has a nonzero nonnegative solution if and only if the following system of strict inequalities is unsatisfiable: for all $(f,g,h) \in \bar{J}$, \begin{equation} \sum_{p \in P}y_p\omega[f,g,h](p)\ >\ 0\,. \end{equation} Consider the case $\tuple{f,g,h}=\tuple{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}$. Then $\omega[f,g,h]=\omega$ and thus $\omega[f,g,h](p)=\omega(p)>0$ for all $p\in {\rm supp}(\omega)\cap P$, by the definition of $P$. Moreover, by~\eqref{eq:Pweights} \begin{equation} \sum_{p\in P}y_p\omega(p) \ =\ \sum_{p_1\in P_1}(y_{p_1}+y_{p_2}+y_{p_3})\omega(p_1)\,, \end{equation} where we denoted (with a slight abuse of notation) by $p_2$ and $p_3$ the related operations of $p_1$. For $\tuple{f,g,h} = \tuple{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}$ the LHS of~\eqref{eq:pixleygordan} is equal to~\eqref{eq:split}. Thus, for~\eqref{eq:pixleygordan} to hold in this case we must have at least one triple of related operations $\tuple{p_1,p_2,p_3} \in J$ with $y_{p_1} + y_{p_2} + y_{p_3} > 0$. Suppose $\tuple{p_1,p_2,p_3}\in J$ is chosen to maximise $y_{p_1} + y_{p_2} + y_{p_3}$. The left-hand side of \eqref{eq:pixleygordan} when $\tuple{f,g,h} = \tuple{p_1,p_2,p_3}$ is equal to \begin{equation} - y_{p_1} - y_{p_2} - y_{p_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s)\,, \end{equation} since $o[p_1,p_2,p_3]$ is equal to a Pixley operation only when $o$ is one of the three projections, which give the first three terms in~\eqref{eq:abc}, or a semiprojection, which gives the last term of~\eqref{eq:abc}, the sum over $S$. We have \begin{equation} \begin{split} \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s)\ =\ & \sum_{s_1\in S_1}y_{s_1[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s_1) + \sum_{s_2\in S_2}y_{s_2[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s_2) + \sum_{s_3\in S_3}y_{s_3[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s_3) \\ =\ & \sum_{\substack{\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}\in S_1\times S_2\times S_3\\s_1,s_2,s_3\mbox{ \scriptsize related}}}(y_{s_1[p_1,p_2,p_3]}+y_{s_2[p_1,p_2,p_3]}+y_{s_3[p_1,p_2,p_3]})\omega(s_1) \\ \leq\ & \frac{\omega(S)}{3}(y_{p_1}+y_{p_2}+y_{p_3}),\\ \end{split} \end{equation} where the first equality follows from the definition of $S$; the second equality follows from fact that $s[p_1,p_2,p_3]$ is a Pixley operation of type $i$ given $s$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, where $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, and hence $\tuple{s_1[p_1,p_2,p_3],s_2[p_1,p_2,p_3],s_3[p_1,p_2,p_3]}$ is a triple of related Pixley operations given that $\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}$ is a triple of related semiprojections; and the last inequality follows from the definition of $w(S)$ and the choice of $(p_1,p_2,p_3)$. Combining~\eqref{eq:abc} and~\eqref{eq:S3}, we have \begin{equation} - y_{p_1} - y_{p_2} - y_{p_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s) \ \leq\ - y_{p_1} - y_{p_2} - y_{p_3} + \frac{w(S)}{3}(y_{p_1}+y_{p_2}+y_{p_3}) \ <\ 0\,, \end{equation} where the last strict inequality follows from $w(S)<3$ since $w(P)>0$ and~\eqref{eq:sum3}. Hence, \eqref{eq:pixleygordan} is unsatisfiable and, by Gordan's Theorem, \eqref{eq:pixleyzero} must have a nonzero nonnegative solution $x^*$. We finish Step~I by using $x^*$ to prove the existence of a weighting in $W$ that assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations. Let \begin{equation} \mu'=\sum_{(f,g,h) \in \bar{J}}x^*_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h]\,, \end{equation} be a weighted sum of superpositions of $\omega$. By the choice of $x^*$, $\mu'$ assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations. From the definition of $\bar{J}$, \begin{equation} \mu'\ =\ x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3]+\sum_{(f,g,h)\in J}x^*_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h]\,. \end{equation} We know that $x^*$ is nonzero and nonnegative. Note that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}=0$ for all $(f,g,h)\in J$ would contradict that $\mu'$ assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations. Let $(f,g,h)\in J$ and $i\in\{1,2,3\}$. Then $o[f,g,h]$ is a Pixley operation of type $i$ if $o$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, $o[f,g,h]$ is a semiprojection of type $i$ if $o$ is a Pixley operation of type $i$, $o[f,g,h]$ is a majority operation if $o$ is a minority operation, and finally $o[f,g,h]$ is a minority operation if $o$ is a majority operation. It follows that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}=0$ would contradict that $\mu'$ assigns zero weight all Pixley operations since Pixley operations of type $i$ would be assigned negative weight since $w(S)-3<0$ as $w(P)>0$. Thus $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}>0$ for at least one $(f,g,h)\in J$. Consequently, $\mu'$ is a nonzero weighting that assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}, $\mu'\in W$.
nodes.statement_short: Obtain a nonzero weighting in $W$ with zero weight on all Pixley operations.

nodes.name: Choose maximising triple
nodes.statement: Suppose $\tuple{p_1,p_2,p_3}\in J$ is chosen to maximise $y_{p_1} + y_{p_2} + y_{p_3}$. The left-hand side of \eqref{eq:pixleygordan} when $\tuple{f,g,h} = \tuple{p_1,p_2,p_3}$ is equal to \begin{equation} - y_{p_1} - y_{p_2} - y_{p_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s)\,, \end{equation} since $o[p_1,p_2,p_3]$ is equal to a Pixley operation only when $o$ is one of the three projections, which give the first three terms in~\eqref{eq:abc}, or a semiprojection, which gives the last term of~\eqref{eq:abc}, the sum over $S$.
nodes.statement_short: Pick the triple maximising the $y$-sum and compute the LHS (23).

nodes.name: Bound the semiprojection term
nodes.statement: We have \begin{equation} \begin{split} \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s)\ =\ & \sum_{s_1\in S_1}y_{s_1[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s_1) + \sum_{s_2\in S_2}y_{s_2[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s_2) + \sum_{s_3\in S_3}y_{s_3[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s_3) \\ =\ & \sum_{\substack{\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}\in S_1\times S_2\times S_3\\s_1,s_2,s_3\mbox{ \scriptsize related}}}(y_{s_1[p_1,p_2,p_3]}+y_{s_2[p_1,p_2,p_3]}+y_{s_3[p_1,p_2,p_3]})\omega(s_1) \\ \leq\ & \frac{\omega(S)}{3}(y_{p_1}+y_{p_2}+y_{p_3}),\\ \end{split} \end{equation} where the first equality follows from the definition of $S$; the second equality follows from fact that $s[p_1,p_2,p_3]$ is a Pixley operation of type $i$ given $s$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, where $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, and hence $\tuple{s_1[p_1,p_2,p_3],s_2[p_1,p_2,p_3],s_3[p_1,p_2,p_3]}$ is a triple of related Pixley operations given that $\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}$ is a triple of related semiprojections; and the last inequality follows from the definition of $w(S)$ and the choice of $(p_1,p_2,p_3)$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the semiprojection contribution by $w(S)/3$ times the maximal $y$-sum (24).

nodes.name: LHS negative
nodes.statement: Combining~\eqref{eq:abc} and~\eqref{eq:S3}, we have \begin{equation} - y_{p_1} - y_{p_2} - y_{p_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s) \ \leq\ - y_{p_1} - y_{p_2} - y_{p_3} + \frac{w(S)}{3}(y_{p_1}+y_{p_2}+y_{p_3}) \ <\ 0\,, \end{equation} where the last strict inequality follows from $w(S)<3$ since $w(P)>0$ and~\eqref{eq:sum3}.
nodes.statement_short: Combining, the LHS is negative since $w(S)<3$.

nodes.name: Gordan gives a solution x*
nodes.statement: Hence, \eqref{eq:pixleygordan} is unsatisfiable and, by Gordan's Theorem, \eqref{eq:pixleyzero} must have a nonzero nonnegative solution $x^*$.
nodes.statement_short: So (21) is infeasible and (20) has a nonzero nonnegative solution $x^*$.

nodes.name: Define mu'
nodes.statement: We finish Step~I by using $x^*$ to prove the existence of a weighting in $W$ that assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations.
nodes.statement_short: Define $\mu'$ from $x^*$; it has zero Pixley weight.

nodes.name: Expand mu'
nodes.statement: From the definition of $\bar{J}$, \begin{equation} \mu'\ =\ x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3]+\sum_{(f,g,h)\in J}x^*_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h]\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Expand $\mu'$ over $\bar J$ (27).

nodes.name: Some J coefficient positive
nodes.statement: We know that $x^*$ is nonzero and nonnegative. Note that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}=0$ for all $(f,g,h)\in J$ would contradict that $\mu'$ assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations.
nodes.statement_short: Not all weight can sit on the identity triple.

nodes.name: Types under superposition with J
nodes.statement: Let $(f,g,h)\in J$ and $i\in\{1,2,3\}$. Then $o[f,g,h]$ is a Pixley operation of type $i$ if $o$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, $o[f,g,h]$ is a semiprojection of type $i$ if $o$ is a Pixley operation of type $i$, $o[f,g,h]$ is a majority operation if $o$ is a minority operation, and finally $o[f,g,h]$ is a minority operation if $o$ is a majority operation.
nodes.statement_short: Superposing with a related Pixley triple swaps semiprojection/Pixley and majority/minority types.

nodes.name: mu' is a nonzero Pixley-free weighting in W
nodes.statement: It follows that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}=0$ would contradict that $\mu'$ assigns zero weight all Pixley operations since Pixley operations of type $i$ would be assigned negative weight since $w(S)-3<0$ as $w(P)>0$. Thus $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}>0$ for at least one $(f,g,h)\in J$. Consequently, $\mu'$ is a nonzero weighting that assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}, $\mu'\in W$.
nodes.statement_short: Identity coefficient positive too, so $\mu'$ is nonzero, Pixley-free and in $W$ by Lemma 3.

nodes.name: Step II: eliminating semiprojections
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step II}: Eliminating semiprojections. We now show how to eliminate semiprojections if needed. If $\mu'$ obtained in Step I assigns positive weight to only semiprojections then we are in case (3) (with $k$=3) of the theorem. Thus let assume that $\mu'$ assigns positive weight to semiprojections and at least one majority or minority operation. By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we can assume the existence of a ternary weighting $\omega\in W$ which assigns weight -1 to all three projections (and thus assigns total positive weight 3). We will use the same notation for $S$, $S_1$, $S_2$, and $S_3$ as before although note that the weighting $\omega$ is now different from the one we had before and throughout Step I. We have $w(S)<3$ and~\eqref{eq:Srelated},~\eqref{eq:Scard},~\eqref{eq:Sweights} still hold for $\omega$. We again use Gordan's Theorem to show that there exists a nonzero ternary weighting in $W$ that assigns positive weight to majority and minority operations only. Let $J=\{(s_1,s_2,s_3)\in S_1\times S_2\times S_3\:|\:\mbox{$s_1, s_2, s_3$ are related}\}$ and $\bar{J}=\{(\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3)\}\cup J$. We consider the following linear system: for all semiprojections $s\in S$, \begin{equation} \sum_{\tuple{f,g,h}\in \bar{J}}x_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h](s)\ =\ 0\,. \end{equation} By Gordan's Theorem,~\eqref{eq:semiprojzero} has a nonzero nonnegative solution if and only if the following system of strict inequalities is unsatisfiable: for all $(f,g,h) \in \bar{J}$, \begin{equation} \sum_{s \in S}y_s\omega[f,g,h](s)\ >\ 0\,. \end{equation} As in Step I, we can argue that~\eqref{eq:semiprojgordan} is unsatisfiable. Consider the case $\tuple{f,g,h}=\tuple{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}$. Then $\omega[f,g,h]=\omega$ and thus $\omega[f,g,h](s)=\omega(s)>0$ for all $s\in{\rm supp}(\omega)\cap S$, by the definition of $S$. Moreover, by~\eqref{eq:Sweights} \begin{equation} \sum_{s\in S}\omega(s)y_s \ =\ \sum_{s_1\in S_1}(y_{s_1}+y_{s_2}+y_{s_3})\omega(s_1)\,, \end{equation} where we denoted by $s_2$ and $s_3$ the related operations of $s_1$. Therefore, for \eqref{eq:semiprojgordan} to hold when $\tuple{f,g,h} = \tuple{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}$ we must have at least one triple of related semiprojections $\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3} \in J$ with $y_{s_1} + y_{s_2} + y_{s_3} > 0$. Suppose $\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}\in J$ is chosen to maximise $y_{s_1} + y_{s_2} + y_{s_3}$. The left-hand side of \eqref{eq:semiprojgordan} when $\tuple{f,g,h} = \tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}$ is equal to \begin{equation} - y_{s_1} - y_{s_2} - y_{s_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s)\,, \end{equation} since $o[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is equal to a semiprojection only when $o$ is one of the three projections, which give the first three terms in~\eqref{eq:Sabc}, or a semiprojection, which gives the last term of~\eqref{eq:Sabc}, the sum over $S$. We have \begin{equation} \begin{split} \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s)\ =\ & \sum_{s_1\in S_1}y_{s_1[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s_1) + \sum_{s_2\in S_2}y_{s_2[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s_2) + \sum_{s_3\in S_3}y_{s_3[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s_3) \\ =\ & \sum_{\substack{\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}\in S_1\times S_2\times S_3\\s_1,s_2,s_3\mbox{\scriptsize related}}}(y_{s_1[s_1,s_2,s_3]}+y_{s_2[s_1,s_2,s_3]}+y_{s_3[s_1,s_2,s_3]})\omega(s_1) \\ \leq\ & \frac{\omega(S)}{3}(y_{s_1}+y_{s_2}+y_{s_3}),\\ \end{split} \end{equation} where the first equality follows from the definition of $S$; the second equality follows from fact that $s[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is a semiprojection of type $i$ given $s$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, where $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, and hence $\tuple{s_1[s_1,s_2,s_3],s_2[s_1,s_2,s_3],s_3[s_1,s_2,s_3]}$ is a triple of related semiprojections given that $\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}$ is a triple of related semiprojections; and the last inequality follows from the definition of $w(S)$ and the choice of $(s_1,s_2,s_3)$. Combining~\eqref{eq:Sabc} and~\eqref{eq:SS3}, we have \begin{equation} - y_{s_1} - y_{s_2} - y_{s_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s) \ \leq\ - y_{s_1} - y_{s_2} - y_{s_3} + \frac{w(S)}{3}(y_{s_1}+y_{s_2}+y_{s_3}) \ <\ 0\,, \end{equation} where the last strict inequality follows from $w(S)<3$. Hence, \eqref{eq:semiprojgordan} is unsatisfiable and, by Gordan's Theorem, \eqref{eq:semiprojzero} must have a nonzero nonnegative solution $x^*$. We finish Step~II by using $x^*$ to prove the existence of a weighting in $W$ that assigns zero weight to all semiprojections. Let \begin{equation} \mu=\sum_{(f,g,h) \in J}\omega[f,g,h]x^*_{f,g,h}\,, \end{equation} be a weighted sum of superpositions of $\omega$. By the choice of $x^*$, $\mu$ assigns zero weight to all semiprojections. From the definition of $\bar{J}$, \begin{equation} \mu\ =\ x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3]+\sum_{(f,g,h) \in J}x^*_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h]\,. \end{equation} We know that $x^*$ is nonzero and nonnegative. Note that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}=0$ for all $(f,g,h)\in J$ would contradict that $\mu'$ assigns zero weight to all semiprojections. Let $(s_1,s_2,s_3)\in J$ and $i\in\{1,2,3\}$. Then $o[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is a semiprojection of type $i$ if $o$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, $o[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is a majority operation if $o$ is a majority operation, and finally $o[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is a minority operation if $o$ is a minority operation. (Note that we do not need to consider the case when $f$ is a Pixley operation as $\omega$ assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations.) It follows that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}=0$ would contradict that $\mu$ assigns zero weight all semiprojections since semiprojections of type $i$ would be assigned negative weight since $w(S)-3<0$ as $\omega$ assigns positive weight to some majority or minority (or possibly both) operations. Thus $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}$ for at least one $(f,g,h)\in J$. Consequently, $\mu$ is a nonzero weighting that assigns zero weight to all semiprojections. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}, $\mu\in W$.
nodes.statement_short: Obtain a nonzero weighting in $W$ with zero weight on all semiprojections.

nodes.statement: It follows that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}=0$ would contradict that $\mu$ assigns zero weight all semiprojections since semiprojections of type $i$ would be assigned negative weight since $w(S)-3<0$ as $\omega$ assigns positive weight to some majority or minority (or possibly both) operations. nodes.name: Step III: majority and minority operations
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step III}: Majority and minority operations. In Steps I and II, we have shown that any weighted clone $W$ with a positive ternary weighting contains a ternary weighting that assigns nonzero weight to semiprojections alone (case~(3) of the theorem with $k=3$), or a mix of majority and minority operations. Finally, we will show that if $W$ contains a weighting $\omega$ that assigns weight to majority and minority operations alone then $W$ also contains a weighting of one of the three types described in cases~(2a),~(2b), and~(2c) of the theorem. Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ denote the sets of majority and minority operations in the support of $\omega$. Suppose that $\omega$ assigns total weight $2+a$ to $M_1$ and total weight $1-a$ to $M_2$ for some $a > 0$. For each $f \in M_2$, we define $\mu_f = \omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,f]$, so $\mu_f$ assigns weight $a$ to $\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1$ and weight $-a$ to $f$. Note that $\mu_f$ is not a proper weighting, since $a > 0$. We obtain a weighting $\mu \in W$ which assigns positive weight to majority operations only as follows: \begin{equation} \mu = \omega + \sum_{f \in M_2}\frac{\omega(f)}{a}\mu_f\,. \end{equation} Similarly, suppose that $\omega$ assigns total weight $2-a$ to $M_1$ and total weight $1+a$ to $M_2$ for some $a>0$. For each $f\in M_1$, we define $\mu_f=\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,f,f]$, so $\mu_f$ assigns weight $a$ to $\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1$ and weight $-a$ to $f$. We obtain a weighting $\mu \in W$ which assigns positive weight to minority operations only as follows: \begin{equation} \mu = \omega + \sum_{f \in M_1}\frac{\omega(f)}{a}\mu_f\,. \end{equation} In both cases $\mu\in W$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}.
nodes.statement_short: Rebalance a majority/minority weighting into one of cases (2a), (2b), (2c).

nodes.name: Goal of Step III
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step III}: Majority and minority operations. In Steps I and II, we have shown that any weighted clone $W$ with a positive ternary weighting contains a ternary weighting that assigns nonzero weight to semiprojections alone (case~(3) of the theorem with $k=3$), or a mix of majority and minority operations. Finally, we will show that if $W$ contains a weighting $\omega$ that assigns weight to majority and minority operations alone then $W$ also contains a weighting of one of the three types described in cases~(2a),~(2b), and~(2c) of the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Steps I-II leave semiprojections only (case 3) or a majority/minority mix.

nodes.name: Majority weight exceeds 2
nodes.statement: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ denote the sets of majority and minority operations in the support of $\omega$. Suppose that $\omega$ assigns total weight $2+a$ to $M_1$ and total weight $1-a$ to $M_2$ for some $a > 0$. For each $f \in M_2$, we define $\mu_f = \omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,f]$, so $\mu_f$ assigns weight $a$ to $\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1$ and weight $-a$ to $f$. Note that $\mu_f$ is not a proper weighting, since $a > 0$. We obtain a weighting $\mu \in W$ which assigns positive weight to majority operations only as follows: \begin{equation} \mu = \omega + \sum_{f \in M_2}\frac{\omega(f)}{a}\mu_f\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: If majority weight is $2+a$, superposing $\omega[e_1,e_1,f]$ removes minority weight: case (2a).

nodes.name: Minority weight exceeds 1
nodes.statement: Similarly, suppose that $\omega$ assigns total weight $2-a$ to $M_1$ and total weight $1+a$ to $M_2$ for some $a>0$. For each $f\in M_1$, we define $\mu_f=\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,f,f]$, so $\mu_f$ assigns weight $a$ to $\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1$ and weight $-a$ to $f$. We obtain a weighting $\mu \in W$ which assigns positive weight to minority operations only as follows: \begin{equation} \mu = \omega + \sum_{f \in M_1}\frac{\omega(f)}{a}\mu_f\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: If minority weight is $1+a$, superposing $\omega[e_1,f,f]$ removes majority weight: case (2b).

nodes.name: Both rebalanced weightings in W
nodes.statement: In both cases $\mu\in W$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3 puts $\mu$ in $W$ in both cases.

nodes.name: Cyclic weighted polymorphism is necessary for tractability
nodes.statement: In recent work on the tractability of valued constraint languages, it has been shown that a necessary condition for tractability is the existence of a \emph{cyclic} weighted polymorphism~\cite{Kozik15:icalp}.\footnote{A $k$-ary operation if \emph{cyclic} if $f(x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_k)=f(x_2,\ldots,x_k,x_1)$ for every $x_1,\ldots,x_k$. A weighting $\omega$ is cyclic if every operation $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ is cyclic.}
conclusions: a necessary condition for tractability is the existence of a \emph{cyclic} weighted polymorphism

nodes.name: Cyclic weighted polymorphism is sufficient under the dichotomy conjecture
nodes.statement: Moreover, it has been also shown that, under the assumption of the dichotomy conjecture of Feder and Vardi for the decision problem, this condition is also sufficient~\cite{Kolmogorov15:general-valued}.
assumptions: under the assumption of the dichotomy conjecture of Feder and Vardi for the decision problem
conclusions: this condition is also sufficient
